explanation: An estuary is a partially enclosed coastal body of water where freshwater from land runoff mixes with seawater. Organisms in estuaries must possess adaptations to survive fluctuating salinity levels. Estuaries are highly productive; nearly two-thirds of all marine fishes and shellfish depend on estuaries for growth and development. Rocky and sandy shores are constantly bombarded by waves. The intertidal zone is the shoreline area situated between high and low tide lines, home to both attached organisms (which anchor to rocks) and unattached organisms.

questions.q: What is an estuary, and why is it ecologically significant for marine life?
opts: A deep ocean zone with hydrothermal vents; it supports chemoautotrophs.
A partially enclosed body of water where fresh water and seawater mix; nearly two-thirds of marine fishes and shellfish require it for development.
A freshwater wetland dominated by woody shrubs; it serves as a carbon reservoir.
An acidic peat bog; it hosts unique carnivorous plant species.

questions.q: What zone lies between the high and low tide levels on rocky and sandy shores?
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Intertidal zone - Lies between high and low tide.'
